title: CloudFront with API Gateway and ALB (dynamic and hybrid origins)
hook: Static assets belong on S3 at the edge, but your REST API still lives on Application Load Balancer (ALB) or Amazon API Gateway. CloudFront can front both — giving you one domain, edge TLS, and AWS WAF — if you treat /api/* as uncached and forward the right headers.

blocks.text: Custom origins let CloudFront proxy dynamic traffic to HTTPS endpoints: Application Load Balancer (ALB) targets in EC2 or Amazon Elastic Container Service (ECS), or Amazon API Gateway (HTTP API or REST API) for serverless. The /api/* cache behavior typically uses CachingDisabled, forwards all viewer headers (especially Host and Authorization), and allows POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE. CloudFront adds latency on cache miss but provides global anycast entry, DDoS mitigation with AWS Shield Standard, and a single ACM certificate for app.example.com serving both static and API paths.

entries.plainDefinition: Non-S3 origin — ALB, API Gateway, or any HTTPS server.
Controls which viewer headers, cookies, and query strings CloudFront sends to the origin.
entries.example: AllViewer policy forwards Host so ALB listener rule matches.

entries.plainDefinition: Layer 7 load balancer routing HTTP requests to targets in a VPC.
entries.example: ECS Fargate service behind HTTPS listener on 443.

entries.plainDefinition: Managed API front door with throttling, auth, and Lambda or HTTP integrations.
entries.example: HTTP API with JWT authorizer integrated with Lambda.

blocks.text: Teams put CloudFront in front of APIs for WAF bot control, geographic blocking, and custom domain TLS — not for caching POST bodies. Misconfiguration causes 502 Bad Gateway (wrong protocol, expired cert on origin), 403 from API Gateway (Host header mismatch), or worse — cached JSON shared across users. Hybrid architectures (SPA on S3, API on ALB) are standard for Angular and React apps; interviews expect you to diagram behaviors and explain why TTL is zero on API paths.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: one distribution, /api/* → ALB or API Gateway with CachingDisabled + AllViewer, static on S3. CloudFront value for APIs = WAF + edge TLS + DDoS, not origin offload.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Viewer POST /api/orders
items.body: TLS terminates at edge; WAF rules evaluate first if attached.

items.title: Behavior matches /api/*
items.body: CachingDisabled — every request forwards to origin (no shared cache risk).

items.title: Origin request includes Host
items.body: ALB listener rule for api.internal.example.com or API Gateway custom domain must match forwarded Host.

items.title: Response returns through edge
items.body: Set-Cookie and Cache-Control: private pass through to browser; not stored at edge.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — ALB origin with API behavior
snippet.code:
Resources:
  HybridDistribution:
    Type: AWS::CloudFront::Distribution
    Properties:
      DistributionConfig:
        Enabled: true
        Origins:
          - Id: S3Static
            DomainName: !GetAtt StaticBucket.RegionalDomainName
            OriginAccessControlId: !GetAtt StaticOAC.Id
            S3OriginConfig:
              OriginAccessIdentity: ''
          - Id: ApiAlb
            DomainName: !GetAtt AppAlb.DNSName
            CustomOriginConfig:
              HTTPSPort: 443
              OriginProtocolPolicy: https-only
              OriginSSLProtocols: [TLSv1.2]
        CacheBehaviors:
          - PathPattern: '/api/*'
            TargetOriginId: ApiAlb
            ViewerProtocolPolicy: https-only
            AllowedMethods:
              - GET
              - HEAD
              - OPTIONS
              - PUT
              - POST
              - PATCH
              - DELETE
            CachedMethods:
              - GET
              - HEAD
            CachePolicyId: 4135ea2d-6df8-44a3-9df3-4b5a84be39ad  # CachingDisabled
            OriginRequestPolicyId: b689b0a8-53d0-40ab-baf2-68738e2966ac  # AllViewer
            Compress: true
        DefaultCacheBehavior:
          TargetOriginId: S3Static
          ViewerProtocolPolicy: redirect-to-https
          CachePolicyId: 658327ea-f89d-4fab-a63d-7e88639e58f6
snippet.explanation: ALB origin uses https-only. API behavior disables cache but allows all methods. AllViewer forwards Host header ALB needs for listener rules.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — API Gateway HTTP API as custom origin
snippet.code:
Resources:
  HttpApi:
    Type: AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Api
    Properties:
      Name: app-http-api
      ProtocolType: HTTP

  ApiDomain:
    Type: AWS::ApiGatewayV2::DomainName
    Properties:
      DomainName: api-origin.internal.example.com
      DomainNameConfigurations:
        - CertificateArn: !Ref InternalCert
          EndpointType: REGIONAL

  CloudFrontApiOrigin:
    Type: AWS::CloudFront::Distribution
    Properties:
      DistributionConfig:
        Origins:
          - Id: HttpApiOrigin
            DomainName: !GetAtt ApiDomain.RegionalDomainName
            CustomOriginConfig:
              HTTPSPort: 443
              OriginProtocolPolicy: https-only
        CacheBehaviors:
          - PathPattern: '/v1/*'
            TargetOriginId: HttpApiOrigin
            CachePolicyId: 4135ea2d-6df8-44a3-9df3-4b5a84be39ad
            OriginRequestPolicyId: b689b0a8-53d0-40ab-baf2-68738e2966ac
snippet.explanation: API Gateway needs a custom domain for stable origin hostname. CloudFront viewer domain (app.example.com) differs from origin domain — Host forwarding is critical.

snippet.label: CLI — smoke test API through CloudFront
snippet.code:
# POST through CloudFront (not direct ALB)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' \
  -X POST 'https://app.example.com/api/health' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer eyJhbG...' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"ping":true}'

# Compare direct ALB (should match status; use internal VPN)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' \
  -X POST 'https://api-alb-123.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com/api/health' \
  -H 'Host: app.example.com'
snippet.explanation: 200 through CloudFront confirms behavior routing and header forwarding. 502 often means SSL or security group; 403 often means Host mismatch on API Gateway.

snippet.label: CLI — CloudFront Function viewer request rewrite (SPA API prefix)
snippet.explanation: CloudFront Functions run at viewer request for sub-millisecond header tweaks. Lambda@Edge needed if you must call AWS APIs or rewrite to a different origin dynamically.

blocks.title: CloudFront API proxy vs dev server proxy
rows: Same origin if SPA and API share domain

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Caching GET /api/users with default policy. Not forwarding Host to API Gateway custom domain. ALB security group allows 0.0.0.0/0 instead of AWS managed prefix list for CloudFront. Using WebSocket through CloudFront to ALB — WebSocket needs separate architecture. Double TLS misconfiguration causing 502.

blocks.text: Choose API Gateway when you want built-in throttling, usage plans, and Lambda integration; choose ALB when you have long-lived containers, WebSocket on separate domain, or gRPC (not via CloudFront). CloudFront to regional API Gateway adds ~extra hop on miss — measure TTFB. How to prove it in production: compare OriginLatency metric with direct ALB access from same region; 502 spike maps to target health or cert expiry. AWS managed prefix list com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing for ALB ingress is tighter than 0.0.0.0/0.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Forward Host; restrict SG to CloudFront prefix list
Custom domain required; stage in Host
Higher latency and cost than HTTP API
Lose edge WAF on API unless separate subdomain

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying CloudFront caches your API for performance without mentioning TTL 0 and auth headers. Strong answer: CloudFront in front of API is for security and single domain; caching only on explicitly public idempotent GETs.

interviewTakeaways: Hybrid distribution: S3 for static, ALB or API Gateway for /api/* with CachingDisabled and AllViewer origin request policy.
Forward Host header — API Gateway and ALB listener rules depend on it; 403/502 often means header or SSL mismatch.
Restrict ALB ingress to CloudFront managed prefix list; never open API port to the entire internet when CloudFront fronts it.
60s: One domain, two origins, API TTL 0, WAF at edge. CloudFront value = TLS + WAF + DDoS, not caching POST.
Follow-up: API Gateway vs ALB as origin — when would you pick each?
commonPitfalls: Enabling cache on authenticated GET /api/me — rejection answer because responses leak across users.
Strong answer: CachingDisabled default for /api/*; optional short TTL only on public read endpoints with explicit cache key.
ALB security group open to 0.0.0.0/0 on 443 bypassing CloudFront protection.
API Gateway 403 because CloudFront sends wrong Host — origin domain must match API custom domain config.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Angular HttpClient and fetch use relative /api when SPA and API share CloudFront domain — no CORS preflight. Absolute ALB URL in bundle breaks when CloudFront is required for WAF.
Dev proxy maps /api to localhost:5000. Production maps same path via CloudFront behavior to ALB. environment.ts must not hardcode internal ALB DNS in client bundle.
